use_case: Face verification (1:1) at employee and staff entrances of 3 customer sites: the reader compares a live face image with the enrolled template of the badge presented
business_owner: Vice President, Remote Operations (operator); each customer decides whether to use it at its building
vendor_or_model: PACS software vendor's face verification module (machine learning face matching), hosted by the company in the IBOP; 11 face-capable readers
build_or_buy: Buy (vendor module, configured and hosted by the company)
data_categories: Face templates (treated as biometric data); enrollment images; badge IDs; match scores; access events
affects_individuals: Yes (1,850 enrolled employees, faculty, staff, and graduate students)
consequential_decision_category: Safety/CI (physical access to government buildings; access to the workplace)
human_in_the_loop: Second factor with the badge only. A failed match falls back to badge plus PIN or the guard desk; no one is refused entry on a face result alone; results are never used for discipline or given to police without the customer's human review
applicable_laws: State breach and biometric laws where enrolled people reside (Florida worked example: Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI), 501.171(2) and (6), and 501.702; whether templates computed from camera images are biometric data is unsettled, counsel to confirm); Fla. Stat. 119.071(5)(g), 119.071(3)(a), and 119.0701 (public records); FERPA 34 CFR 99.33(a) for student templates at site P2; FTC Act Section 5 (claims); state cybersecurity exhibits (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate)
status: Pilot at 3 sites; continues for enrolled volunteers with conditions (section 10); no new enrollments
committee_review: Reviewed 2026-08-26 (pilots had started on customer orders in 2026-02 to 2026-04)
bias_testing_status: Vendor data plus an initial screen of site P1 logs (disparity flagged); local testing with impostor tests due 2027-03-31
monitoring: Monthly FNMR by site; quarterly FNMR by group; monthly template retention reconciliation

use_case: Face identification (1:N) of people in the public lobbies of a county government center against a county watch list (county request, 2026-06)
vendor_or_model: Same PACS and video vendor (proposed identification feature)
data_categories: Face images of members of the public; watch list images
affects_individuals: Yes (members of the public using county services)
consequential_decision_category: Government services (access to essential government services); Safety/CI
human_in_the_loop: Proposed design: alerts to guards; no review, correction, or appeal process
applicable_laws: State biometric and breach laws (Florida worked example: Fla. Stat. 501.171 and 501.702); Fla. Stat. 119.071 and 119.0701; FTC Act Section 5; customer counsel review required
status: Not approved: the company declined to configure or operate it
monitoring: Customer requests logged by the GRC team

use_case: ROC alarm prioritization: a machine learning score orders the alarm queue and groups likely nuisance alarms; no alarm is suppressed
vendor_or_model: Alarm automation software vendor's machine learning feature, tuned on the company's alarm history
data_categories: Alarm events; building and device metadata; operator dispositions (operator IDs only)
affects_individuals: Indirectly (building occupants depend on alarm response)
human_in_the_loop: Operators see and acknowledge every alarm; fire, duress, and forced-door alarms are pinned to the top by fixed rules outside the model; operators can re-order the queue
applicable_laws: Customer contract alarm response service levels; state cybersecurity exhibits (SI-4)
bias_testing_status: Not applicable to individuals; ranking accuracy checked by segment and building age
monitoring: Weekly check that no confirmed true alarm waited more than 5 minutes because of ranking; monthly wrong-grouping rate
linked_risks_and_poam: Portfolio review only (no separate P01 risk)

use_case: Video analytics (person and vehicle detection, line crossing, loitering) in customer video systems at 186 buildings, sending alerts to customer guards and ROC operators
vendor_or_model: Video management software vendor's analytics module and camera-embedded analytics
data_categories: Live and recorded video of people and vehicles; alert metadata
affects_individuals: Yes (building occupants and visitors are recorded and analyzed)
consequential_decision_category: Safety/CI (security alerting); no decisions about individuals
human_in_the_loop: An operator or guard checks the video before any response; analytics never trigger door or lockdown actions; face recognition functions are to be confirmed disabled at every site
applicable_laws: State laws where the customer is located (counsel); customer orders and use limits; Fla. Stat. 119.071(3)(a) for security system records (worked example)
status: In production (AQ-1 installed base plus new Security Integration projects)
biometric_data: No (to be confirmed at every site)
monitoring: Annual customer purpose attestation (planned); false alert rate per site

use_case: License plate recognition at the entrances of 9 county and university parking garages: plates matched to the permit list open the gate; hotlist alerting disabled
vendor_or_model: License plate recognition camera vendor integrated with the PACS
data_categories: Plate images; plate numbers; timestamps; permit lists
human_in_the_loop: Drivers without a read use the card reader or intercom; the gate never closes on a vehicle because of a read; plate data goes to law enforcement only on a customer request through PRC-04.1
applicable_laws: State laws on license plate data where the customer is located (counsel to confirm by state); customer orders; public records duties (Fla. Stat. 119.0701 worked example)
bias_testing_status: Not started (read accuracy by plate type and issuing state)
monitoring: Monthly read accuracy sample; retention check against customer orders

use_case: Fault detection and diagnostics on BAS trend data that proposes maintenance work orders
vendor_or_model: Company-built rules and a vendor analytics library on the data platform (Cloud provider B)
data_categories: BAS trend data (temperatures, valve positions, energy use); no personal data
human_in_the_loop: Technicians confirm every suggested fault before any work; advisory only, with no writes to building systems
monitoring: Monthly share of suggested faults confirmed by technicians

use_case: Closed-loop HVAC optimization pilot that writes supervisory chilled water and air handler setpoints at 12 state and university buildings
vendor_or_model: HVAC optimization software vendor (machine learning supervisory control) that reads trend data from the data platform (P05 BP-17) and writes through the IBOP BAS supervisory servers
data_categories: BAS trend data; weather; occupancy schedules
human_in_the_loop: Writes only inside setpoint bounds enforced by the BAS, not by the model; operators can override at the ROC or the building; the building falls back to its own schedule if the signal is lost; no writes to life-safety, smoke control, or laboratory exhaust systems
applicable_laws: Customer orders and contract terms; state cybersecurity exhibits (CM-3, SI-10)
bias_testing_status: Not applicable to individuals; comfort complaints reviewed by building
monitoring: Monthly count of blocked out-of-bounds writes; monthly comfort complaint review

use_case: Work order triage in the Facility Services Portal: a model suggests priority and trade for incoming service requests
vendor_or_model: Company-built on a cloud AI service (Cloud provider B) under terms with no training on company data
data_categories: Service request text; building and asset data; requester contact details; FCI in federal work orders
human_in_the_loop: Dispatchers confirm priority and trade for every request; leaks, entrapments, and security events are routed by fixed rules
applicable_laws: FAR 52.204-21 (FCI in federal work orders); customer service levels; SOC 2 SL-2 Processing Integrity (P09)
physical_safety_or_ci_effect: Indirectly (an urgent request could be under-prioritized)
bias_testing_status: Not applicable to individuals; priority accuracy checked by segment
monitoring: Monthly sample of 200 requests; dispatcher override rate

use_case: SOC alert triage assistant that summarizes alerts and suggests dispositions
vendor_or_model: Security tooling vendor's feature (switched on by a vendor release in 2026-05)
data_categories: Security logs and alerts (may contain fragments of personal data)
applicable_laws: State cybersecurity exhibits (IR-4, SI-4); vendor contract terms

use_case: Enterprise generative AI assistant for drafting and summarizing, in an approved tenant (about 4,200 users)
vendor_or_model: Enterprise generative AI service under contract terms with no training on company data
data_categories: Documents and email; Restricted data allowed except CUI and face templates (POL-04 4.8)
human_in_the_loop: Users review all outputs; prohibited for decisions about individuals and for customer security system designs
applicable_laws: POL-04 4.8; 32 CFR Part 2002 (CUI stays in the CUI enclave); customer confidentiality terms; NIST AI 600-1 (guidance)
monitoring: Usage and data loss prevention monitoring; blocked uploads to unapproved AI services

use_case: Applicant resume screening and ranking for technician and trades hiring
vendor_or_model: HR software suite feature (enabled in 2026-02 without review)
human_in_the_loop: Recruiters review all applicants; ranking switched off 2026-08-20
applicable_laws: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act (disparate impact, 42 U.S.C. 2000e-2(k)); 29 CFR 1607.4(D) four-fifths rule as a screen; ADA; state fair employment laws where applicants live (counsel)
bias_testing_status: Not started (adverse impact analysis required before any re-enable)
monitoring: HR confirms monthly that ranking stays disabled

use_case: Generative AI technician assistant in the FSP mobile app that answers troubleshooting questions from equipment manuals and work order history (pilot)
vendor_or_model: Company-built on a cloud AI service foundation model (Cloud provider B) with retrieval from manuals and work orders
data_categories: Equipment manuals; work order history (includes FCI in federal work orders); technician prompts and photos that may show drawings
human_in_the_loop: Technicians follow the manufacturer manual and lockout/tagout procedures; answers cite their sources; the assistant cannot write to building systems
applicable_laws: FAR 52.204-21 (FCI); 32 CFR Part 2002 (no CUI uploads); POL-04 4.8; NIST AI 600-1 (guidance)
physical_safety_or_ci_effect: Indirectly (a wrong procedure could damage equipment)
bias_testing_status: Not applicable (staff tool); answer accuracy sample
monitoring: Weekly answer accuracy sample; blocked photo uploads of marked drawings
